build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player or energy core moves one tile at a time on a visible grid, respecting walls and blocked cells. Score 0 if movement is unconstrained, free-floating, or ignores obstacles.
Same-polarity repulsion pushes magnetic objects away and opposite-polarity attraction pulls them toward the player or source. Score 0 if magnetism is cosmetic or objects only move by direct pushing.
The player can flip polarity or activate a magnetic state change, and this visibly alters how nearby objects respond on the next interaction. Score 0 if there is no player-controlled polarity toggle.

Switches, pressure plates, or gates react when the correct magnetic object reaches them, visibly opening paths or changing the level layout. Score 0 if the only goal is walking to an exit with no interactive puzzle elements.

At least three distinct levels or scenarios demonstrate different puzzle layouts combining push, pull, polarity swap, gates, hazards, or multi-step sequences. Score 0 if every puzzle is the same single-room layout.
At least one puzzle requires a multi-step sequence where an early move sets up a later gate opening, safe path, or chain reaction. Score 0 if all puzzles solve in one obvious move.

Polarity state is visible on the player and on magnetic objects using distinct indicators such as color coding, plus/minus symbols, arrows, or field lines. Score 0 if polarity is hidden and the player must guess.
Normal startup shows a styled title screen with the game name, a Start control, and laboratory or magnet imagery. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI with no theme.

The HUD shows the current level identity, move count or step counter, and puzzle objective so the player always knows what to solve and how far along they are. Score 0 if no contextual information is visible during play.

Undo or reset is available and visibly restores a previous or initial puzzle state without restarting the executable. Completion and failure states show styled screens with next-level, retry, or title navigation. Score 0 if mistakes force a full restart or completion has no feedback.

The laboratory art direction is coherent across grid tiles, magnets, gates, hazards, HUD, title, and result screens, forming a unified visual language. Score 0 if dominated by default controls or unthemed rectangles. Score 0.5 at most when visuals are dominated by primitive shapes, mismatched assets, noisy color choices, or layouts that feel assembled rather than art-directed. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

Magnetic interactions have readable animation or effects: field lines, push/pull motion, polarity flashes, gate sliding, sparks, or particle trails that communicate what just happened. Score 0 if all state changes snap silently with no visual feedback. Score 0.5 at most when feedback exists but is minimal, debug-like, or disconnected from the laboratory theme.
